answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is vested payouts: rewards earned by an agent are locked and released gradually over many epochs, like a vine growing slowly rather than a zephyr blowing through. A flash-farm operator spinning up thousands of fake island identities collects almost nothing before abandoning them, since unvested balances are forfeited on exit. Profitable attack requires keeping each identity active and honest for months, so the cost of running sybils exceeds the yield and the attack economics collapse.
